The graph of a function $y=f(x)$ is shown above. Given $g(t)={\int }_{0}^{t}f(x)\,\text{d}x,$ determine the value of $g(3).$
question.worked_solution:
Evaluating $g(t)$ at $t=3,$ we get the following definite integral:

$$
g(3)={\int }_{0}^{3}f(x)\,\text{d}x
$$

This integral gives the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14284204/assets/b5becb438f3bc8ab5445e116ddb64bf168013301838231bdc4d32d34283da5f1.png)

Note that the graph above consists of $2$ parts:

- $x\in [0,1],$ for which the region between the curve and the $x$-axis is a trapezoid. This corresponds to the area ${A}_{1}.$

- $x\in [1,3],$ for which the region between the curve and the $x$-axis is another trapezoid. This corresponds to the area ${A}_{2}.$

Therefore, we can write the integral as follows:

$$
g(2)={\int }_{0}^{3}f(x)\,\text{d}x={{{\int }_{0}^{1}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{{A}_{1}}+{{{\int }_{1}^{3}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{{A}_{2}}
$$

Now, let's compute these integrals:

- To find the first integral where $x\in [0,1],$ we compute the area ${A}_{1}$ of the trapezoid as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{1} & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot 1\cdot (2+3) \\  & =\frac{5}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

- To find the second integral where $x\in [1,3],$ we compute the area ${A}_{2}$ of the triapezoid as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{2} & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot 2\cdot (2+3) \\  & =5\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}g(2) & ={\int }_{0}^{3}f(x)\,\text{d}x={A}_{1}+{A}_{2}=\frac{5}{2}+5=\frac{15}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
